title: in-depth session Cramer's Ma
text:
in-depth session   TV   
Cramer said that big decline days like Wednesday should not be for panicking, but instead, for patience and buying high-quality stocks on weakness. The Mad Money host spoke about his days as a fund manager, where his boss used to make him wear a Post-it note of shame for missing an opportunity to buy a stock at cheap prices. Wednesday was such day for three high-quality stocks - Boeing (NYSE: BA ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ).
"Many of us should be wearing a collective Post-it if you sold these stocks during the big panic. Remember, if you have conviction, if you believe in a company, you use the declines that we had today to buy the stock, not to sell the stock," Cramer emphasized.
Boeing is a company that has an order book spanning over 20 years. A little uptick in interest rates will not affect that. Since 80% of people in the world have never flown in a plane, this just means there is room for Boeing to grow. The company is also buying its own stock, which just makes it more rewarding for shareholders. The stock is headed to $400.
Amazon, on the other hand, is taking over online retail and grocery business, along with growth in cloud business. Millions of customers across the globe are using Amazon Prime, and wage inflation will not change that. "Did you get washed out of Amazon because you heard that Fed chief Jay Powell might be a little worried that the economy's too hot? That's called a mistake. That's why you need conviction, so you can stick to your guns," said Cramer.
Lastly, it was the big fish - Apple - that had gone down, as analysts were worried about iPhone sales. The stock just made all-time highs after that. "Apple is a consumer product company with an incredible following that's created a beloved technological ecosystem, second to none, with the highest customer loyalty of any device in history," Cramer said. All other consumer stocks that are not close to Apple in terms of loyalty are trading at a premium. This stock should be covered by consumer analysts and not tech analysts. Don't make the mistake of selling it.
